title: Canonical presentation filtration equals the image predicate
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $K$ a bounded-below complex of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $T$ a Cartan--Eilenberg hypercohomology presentation [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation]. For all integers $p,q$ and $x\in H^p(X,K)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], the image-filtration predicate [lem-weil-pbc-etale-hypercohomology-filtration-zero] holds if and only if $x$ is in the image of the canonical inclusion of the $q$-th step of $T.H(p)$.

source.place: Lemma 13.21.3, first spectral sequence and finite induced filtration; Tag 0EZM, proof of Lemma 59.52.1, uniform support bound

proof.text: Set e=embeddingUpIntGE(q). For any supported witness S, its stupid-truncation inclusion is invertible. The chain map inv(ι_S) followed by stupidTruncMap(f) factors f through ι_K by naturality. Applying derived cohomology gives a preimage in the fixed truncation. Conversely the fixed truncation is zero below q, so its inclusion is itself an admissible witness. This proves equivalence of the predicate with the range of H^p(RΓ(ι_K)). The Lean proof uses the existing upstream stupid-truncation API and Mathlib support and functoriality lemmas.

Apply the filtered-step cohomology comparison to obtain an isomorphism from H^p((T.L).step q) to H^p(RΓ(σ_{≥q}K)) with the specified inclusion square. Expand T.H_formula. Image pushforward is the image of the composition; precomposition by the epimorphism onto the image removes its factorization, and precomposition by the comparison isomorphism leaves the image unchanged. Thus (T.H p).step q is the image subobject of H^p(RΓ(ι_K)).

In AddCommGrpCat the epimorphism factorThruImageSubobject is surjective. Therefore an element has a preimage under the image-subobject arrow if and only if it has a preimage under the original map. Apply this to the image equality of the previous step and the range equivalence of the first step.
